4. Autonomy, approvals and automation

Qline can act for you: send email, post to Slack, create calendar events, files, contacts and invoice drafts, and run workflows and missions. You control how much it can do through autonomy levels, approvals, budgets and the emergency stop.

  • Actions taken through your account are your actions. This includes actions you approve and actions that run without a fresh approval because you or your organisation turned on a higher autonomy level, autopilot, a schedule or a workflow.
  • Turning on autopilot or full autonomy is your choice. Messages Qline reads, such as incoming email, can contain instructions written to mislead an AI. Use higher autonomy only where a mistake would be acceptable, and review the activity and audit logs.
  • Publishing to Facebook and changing code on GitHub always need a person's approval in Qline. You are responsible for checking what you approve.
  • If something goes wrong, use the emergency stop and contact us. We cannot undo actions already completed in another service (for example, an email that has been sent).
